newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields edging towards rate cut lows.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields edging towards rate cut lows.

text.p: *Australian bond yields continued to edge towards the lows seen immediately after last Friday's rate cut, led down by the short end of the curve.
*Q1 capex rises 6.5 percent vs forecast 3.5 percent.
Australian bond yields continued to edge towards the lows seen immediately after last Friday's interest rate cut, led down by the short end of the curve.

Traders said that the three-year part of curve had been showing some value, given that at the start of the day it was 100 basis points adrift from official interest rates, now at 5.5 percent, and this was helping to drag the long end with it.
News that March quarter capital expenditure growth came in at the top end of expectations at 6.5 percent, and compared with median forecasts for a 3.5 percent rise, failed to daunt the market.
The second estimate for business investment intentions for 1997/98 included in the data was A$36.57 billion, up from a substantially revised-down A$31.90 billion first estimate.

"The super strong investment climate that seemed to be still prevailing up until this release came out might just be dampened a bit. So far as the bond market, it shouldn't hurt it at all," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia.

"Even though we have 6.5 percent for the quarter and we are all now reasonably confident that the first quarter GDP will be strong, it's the outlook that matters and that's been revised down a bit," he added.

The firm tone saw spreads to the dollar bloc narrow, and the three-year differential to the U.S. close in on parity again, having briefly tested it in immediate reaction on the rate cut on Friday. With the emphasis on short end, the local yield curve steepened slightly once again.
The 10-year bond contract is close to testing resistance at 92.480 after overcoming 92.410 in early trading. The contract briefly touched a 12-week high of 92.500 last Friday.
